Welcome to Al-Falah School
Al-Falah Primary School serves families from across London. Our pupils are bonded by Islamic teachings, and the rich ethnic diversity within our school helps every child develop a deep understanding and respect for one another.
Our aims, vision and ethos are centred on instilling strong Islamic values and raising the educational standards of children in Britain — so they become lifelong learners and leaders who contribute to society. We welcome the challenge of providing every pupil with the knowledge and skills to succeed during their time at Al-Falah and beyond.
Our Values
We strive for FALAH — true success in this world and the next.
Faith
A firm grounding in Islamic belief and love of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.
Akhlaq
Excellent character, manners and respect for self, others and community.
Learning
A passion for knowledge and academic excellence across every subject.
Ambition
High expectations and the confidence to achieve goals in this life and the next.
Hifz
Treasuring the Quran through recitation, memorisation and lifelong devotion.

Welcome
A warm welcome from the Head Teacher
Assalamu Alaikum and a warm welcome to Al-Falah Primary School.
We are an independent Islamic primary school in the heart of Hackney, London, serving children from Year 1 through to Year 6. Our pupils come from many ethnic backgrounds across the city, bonded together by shared Islamic teachings and a genuine love of learning.
At Al-Falah, our aim is simple: to provide every child with the highest quality education — academically, spiritually and morally — within a nurturing, ambitious and safe environment. We hold high expectations of every pupil, and we work in close partnership with parents so that each child reaches their full potential.
Our most recent Ofsted inspection (July 2024) judged us as Good overall, with Outstanding ratings for both Behaviour & Attitudes and Personal Development.
If you are considering Al-Falah for your child, I warmly invite you to visit us. Please contact the school office to arrange an appointment.
M.A Hussain Head Teacher

History
The story of Al-Falah Primary School
Serving Hackney's Muslim community
Al-Falah Primary School was established to provide families in East London with a high-quality independent Islamic primary education — a place where pupils could thrive academically while developing a strong grounding in their faith.
From small beginnings, the school has grown steadily into the recognised institution it is today.
A trusted school
Over the years, Al-Falah has earned the trust of generations of families in Hackney and surrounding boroughs.
Looking forward
While honouring our roots, we continue to look ahead — investing in our curriculum, facilities and staff.

Curriculum
A broad, balanced education combining academic excellence and Islamic learning
Al-Falah delivers a broad and balanced curriculum through the full delivery of the National Curriculum alongside our Islamic studies programme. Our structured planning and ongoing monitoring ensure progression and continuity of learning for every pupil from Year 1 through to Year 6.
Key Stages
National Curriculum Subjects
English
Reading, writing, spelling, grammar and oracy — building confident communicators.
Mathematics
Number, reasoning and problem-solving with strong mental and written fluency.
Science
Enquiry-based learning across biology, chemistry and physics topics.
Computing & ICT
Digital literacy, coding and safe, purposeful use of technology.
Design & Technology
Designing, making and evaluating practical projects.
History
Exploring British and world history to build curiosity and perspective.
Geography
The world's places, people, environments and our role within them.
Art & Design
Creative expression, drawing, painting and exploration of artistic styles.
Physical Education
Active, healthy lifestyles built through sport and movement.
Modern Foreign Language — Arabic
Spoken and written Arabic, opening doors to Quranic understanding.
PSHE
Personal, social, health and economic education for life beyond school.
Learning in Action
A glimpse of pupils' work and activities across the curriculum.
